title: Graduate - Babyzone
descriptionHtml:
Graduate Programme — Babyzone

  • Are you torn between the excitement of start-ups and the stability of corporate life? 
  • Are you keen to continue learning and developing skills whilst experiencing how to build businesses?
  • Are you looking for a role that will offer the opportunity to experience first-hand how a tech company is built, and be supported while taking ownership of work that matters? 

If this sounds like you and you are up for the challenge, we would love to hear from you!

We are looking to hire high-energy, entrepreneurial and value-adding graduate talent to join Blenheim Chalcot in a role dedicated entirely to Babyzone, one of the social-impact organisations supported by BC.

ABOUT US

At Blenheim Chalcot, we invest more than just funds. We invest our knowledge and experience, our ideas and infrastructure. Our ventures are at the forefront of a multitude of industries being disrupted by digital including FinTech, EdTech, GovTech, Media, Sport, Charity and more. We are highly entrepreneurial and seek opportunities where digital technologies can disrupt major markets - ventures we have built include ClearScore, Salary Finance, Modulr and the Rajasthan Royals cricket team.

Many of the companies within the portfolio have materialised from ideas conceived and launched by us, and we have over 4,000 employees to support their growth and development. Our assets under management stand at more than £1.8bn and total portfolio revenue is over £500 million.

We work closely with investment and strategic partners ranging from Paypal, FIS, L&G, Tencent, Experian, Google, WorldPay, Imperial College and some of the leading venture capital and private equity companies internationally.

Our central team, Venture Builder Services (VBS), exists to support our ventures to be successful quickly, sustainably and with access to the best practice tools, solutions, and expertise. We provide a range of services to help new business get off the ground, including technology, growth (marketing and sales), talent, finance, legal and tax.

 IMPACT BEYOND PROFIT

15% of our partnerships and ventures are charities. These include the British Asian Trust, Babyzone and Onside Youth Zones. In the same way that we support our ventures, our Partners provide direct hands-on support to these charities by being active board members and offering expert advice.

ABOUT BABYZONE

Babyzone is an innovative and fast-growing UK early childhood charity. It runs free, open-access community hubs for families with children aged 0-5 in areas of high deprivation, bringing together services, programmes and partners to improve outcomes for young children and their families.

 THE GRADUATE OPPORTUNITY

Joining Blenheim Chalcot as a Graduate, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced and progressive environment while working exclusively with Babyzone. You will be embedded within the Babyzone team and contribute to meaningful projects that support the charity's growth, operations and impact, while benefiting from Blenheim Chalcot's learning, development and employee benefits.

For you as a graduate, this opportunity involves:

  • Dedicated to Babyzone – although you will be employed by Blenheim Chalcot, your role will sit fully within Babyzone. Your day-to-day work, projects and objectives will be focused entirely on supporting Babyzone and its mission, giving you the opportunity to build deep experience within a fast-growing, mission-led organisation.
  • Training & Development – we pride ourselves on having an intentional and continuous learning and development culture at Blenheim Chalcot. You will have access to BC learning and development opportunities designed to strengthen your core professional, commercial and leadership skills, while applying that learning directly to your work at Babyzone. You will learn by doing, taking on real responsibility and developing quickly within the Babyzone team.
  • Early Careers Development – as a BC graduate, you will have access to structured development opportunities designed for those early in their careers. These will support your professional growth while your role itself remains fully dedicated to Babyzone.
  • Graduate Community – you will be part of the wider BC graduate community, with access to relevant learning sessions, networking opportunities and socials. This community is intended to support your development and connection with fellow graduates; your substantive role and day-to-day responsibilities will remain entirely within Babyzone.
  • Accountability – you will be given meaningful responsibility from the outset and supported to take ownership of work that matters. Rather than rotating between businesses, you will build continuity and depth within Babyzone, seeing the direct impact of your work on the organisation and the families and communities it serves.

ARE YOU BC? 

We are not expecting you to have worked in start-ups before or to have studied a tech related degree. For us, it is about hiring the right person and their potential, not just their experience. As such, we are looking for graduates from any discipline – different areas of expertise are great for new perspectives. 

We look for some key fundamentals in people when hiring into the BC Group. We look for people who are:

  • Curious – people in BC are inquisitive, they want to understand ‘why’ and consider if there is a better approach rather than take on the ‘it’s how we’ve always done it’ perspective. Given our ethos is all about disrupting industries with new methods and products, curiosity is at the heart of what we do.
  • ‘Doers’ – surprisingly, this is not a given in a lot of working environments; we are a community of pro-active self-starters. We will provide full support to our graduates, though we do look for proactive people who can use their initiative and drive on a daily basis. Working in an environment where everyone has this trait is incredibly refreshing and we strive to maintain it.
  • Flexible Mindset – working in a growth business environment is ambiguous, diverse and, at times, chaotic by definition. Being adaptable and recognising the importance of flexibility to add value in a constantly evolving company is vital for us.
  • Enthusiasm – you do not need to be a ‘techy’ at heart to work in our environment. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic about what digitalisation is doing to industries and a drive to work in a pioneering sector which represents that drive. A desire for doing new and challenging things makes coming into work a whole lot more fun.
  • Humble & Sociable – building a tech start-up is never easy. As such, we have a ‘no-ego’ policy and seek out people who bring energy to a team, not drain it. We have a down-to-earth and personable culture; we solve complex problems but do not take ourselves too seriously and look to have fun whilst doing so.

If you see yourself in this and would like to work with similarly minded people, we would love to hear from you!

WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU AS A BC EMPLOYEE:

  • Be part of the UK’s leading digital venture builder and have the opportunity to be a part of and learn from the incredible talent in BC
  • Be exposed to the right mix of challenges and learning and development opportunities while building deep, hands-on experience within Babyzone
  • A fun and open, if a little cricket obsessed, atmosphere
  • Discretionary bonus
  • 25 days of paid holidays + your birthday off
  • Life Assurance, Pension Scheme, Cycle to Work Scheme
  • Flexible Benefits including Private Medical and Dental, Gym Subsidiaries

APPLICATION & PROCESS

If you are keen to apply, please submit your CV and a member of our Talent Team will contact you with next steps. We have a rigorous recruitment process, which we use for all our roles to ensure we attract the very best talent. 

We have a three-stage process that will consist of the following:

Stage 1: Telephone interview with a member of the BC Talent team

Stage 2: Virtual assessment day, consisting of both individual and group activities

Stage 3: Final interviews with Blenheim Chalcot and Babyzone at Scale Space, White City

*Please note the timeframes provided above are subject to change, which we will communicate throughout the process*

Blenheim Chalcot is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. Diversity is one of our core values, thus making it core to our business. We strive to maximise the diversity of our workforce and welcome applications from everyone. We encourage diversity through perspective, background, identity, and thought whilst also fostering an environment where everyone can express themselves regardless of your race, religion, sex, gender, colour, national origin, disability, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic. We are committed to continuing to nurture an inclusive environment and building a diverse workforce.

By submitting your CV you understand that we have a legitimate interest to use your personal data for the purposes of assessing your eligibility for this role.  This means that we may use your personal data to contact you to discuss your CV or arrange an interview, or transfer your CV to the hiring manager(s) of the role you have applied for.  You can ask us at any time to remove your CV from our database by emailing  here.

title: Ground Software Engineer - Core

Dimension Business :

  • Pilote le niveau de préférence et de mindshare de nos partenaires à notre égard : positionne VML Consulting comme partenaire de référence dans leur écosystème, fait progresser notre niveau de partenariat et suit la performance des objectifs conjoints,

Vous justifiez de 5 à 10 ans d’expérience, dont une expérience significative en alliances / partenariats technologiques, channel ou business development – idéalement acquise en cabinet de conseil, ESN, agence ou chez un éditeur / hyperscaler.

Votre rigueur et votre curiosité font de vous un acteur à la fois à l’aise dans la logique de développement business sur des clients existants que sur de la conquête opportuniste, ou en relai d’un partenaire.

La maîtrise de l’anglais, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, est indispensable : vous adressez des partenaires et des interlocuteurs internationaux de manière totalement autonome.

Wenn du dich bei uns bewirbst möchten wir ein Loom Video von dir erhalten. 🙏🏻

Was ist Loom und brauche ich einen Account? Loom ist ein kostenloses Tool, mit dem du dich selbst und/oder deinen Bildschirm aufnimmst und per Link teilst. Die kostenlose Version reicht völlig. Du kannst auch jedes andere Tool nutzen (z. B. Handyvideo über Google Drive) Hauptsache, wir können den Link öffnen.

Wie lang sollte das Video sein? 2–4 Minuten. Kürzer ist besser als länger – wenn du es knapp auf den Punkt bringst, ist das schon ein Pluspunkt.

Was soll ich im Video sagen? Stell dich kurz vor, erzähl, warum du zu RealStudio willst, und zeig uns ein Projekt, einen Kunden oder ein Ergebnis, auf das du stolz bist. Gerne mit geteiltem Bildschirm, z. B. Kampagnen, Reportings oder Content, an dem du beteiligt warst.

Muss das Video professionell aussehen? Nein. Kein Schnitt, keine Musik, kein Skript nötig. Wir bewerten nicht die Videoqualität, sondern dich. Ein ruhiger Ort und guter Ton reichen.

Auf Deutsch oder Englisch? Bitte auf Deutsch, da unsere Kunden überwiegend aus dem DACH-Raum kommen.

Wer sieht mein Video? Nur die Personen, die bei uns am Bewerbungsprozess beteiligt sind. Wir teilen es nicht weiter und löschen es nach Abschluss des Verfahrens.

Wie geht es nach dem Video weiter? Wir melden uns innerhalb von max 2 Werktagen bei dir. Wenn es passt, folgt ein Kennenlern-Call und danach ein Probetag, an dem du an einer realistischen Aufgabe mit uns arbeitest.

title: Head of Capital
descriptionHtml:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The opportunity

We are looking for a Head of Capital to run how Relay raises equity and works with its investors: the next round and the ones after it, from the investor map to the close, next to the CEO.

Relay is a technology enabled parcel carrier - we deliver parcels from retailers to end customers but do it much more efficiently than incumbents. This efficiency has propelled us into one of the fastest growing companies in Europe - we have grown over 40x in the last 18 months. The capital Relay raises decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Raising it well, from the right investors, on terms we understand, is a job in its own right.

About the role

The capital we raise next decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Our next round is planned for Q2/Q3 2027. It is for growth, from growth-stage investors, and it will be won on evidence. Today a raise runs through the CEO and the CFO alongside their day jobs. It works. It is however, not a system.

You will be the person who makes it one. You will not just be the person who holds and runs the Series C transaction, but also be the Head of the Office that will build the systems to raise multiple rounds of capital in the future. Between rounds you keep the map, the materials and the investors warm, so each raise starts from a record, not a blank page. Few roles let you own how a growing company raises the capital it runs on, from the inside, round after round.

Who you work with

  • CEO: you report here. The CEO pitches and takes the decisions on a round.

  • CFO: you work together daily. The CFO owns the budget, the forecast, internal finance and any debt. You own equity, the investors behind it, and the investor-facing model built from the CFO's numbers — never a second set.

  • Co-founder and the Extended Leadership Team: the proof a round needs.

  • External & Internal Counsel: terms and the close.

  • Board: updates between rounds and approval on the round.

What you'll do

Running the transaction with the CEO & CFO

  1. Build the investor map: which funds, which partner at each, why each fits us, in what order we go, and the warm path to each.

  2. The process start to close: the timeline, outreach, a brief before every meeting and notes after, investor questions answered within a day, and diligence.

  3. Put term sheets side by side and show what each costs in the round after. Draw up illustrative analysis and counsel the CEO on the right strategy.

  4. Hold the story in one version, drafted with the CEO. The same claims and numbers across the deck, the model and the data room.

  5. Own the investor-facing model: scenarios, unit economics and use of funds. Every number ties to one the CFO has signed.

Between rounds

  1. Refresh the deck, the KPI pack and the data room every quarter.

  2. Write investor and board updates. Answer existing investors' questions. Track what we promised them.

  3. Build relationships with investors so you can source your own relationships for future rounds

  4. Read the market: who invests at our stage, on what terms, and what comparable companies showed when they raised. Put what Relay must show, and by when, to the leadership team in writing.

Across both

  1. Agree in writing with each function what it produces for a raise and by when. Flag the proof the story needs a quarter early, not the week before.

  2. Keep the record: what each investor asked, what we answered, what we promised and what we learned.

By the end of your first six months

  • An investor map with a reason beside every name.

  • One version of the story across the deck, the model and the data room.

  • A data room refreshed every quarter, never rebuilt.

  • A written agreement with each function on what it produces for a raise.

  • A clear line of sight to a closed round from a ranked list of investors.

What we're looking for

You have run a growth-stage equity round from inside a company, or worked on several from the investing side. You want to own the process, with a view to owning the pitch and fundraising function in the future as the company scales.

We don't ask for a set number of years or a particular firm on your CV. We ask for evidence. Be ready to walk us through specific rounds and your part in them.

Required

  • Round experience: you ran an equity round from inside a company, or worked on several as an investor. You can show the map you built, the order you ran it in and what you would change.

  • Investor writing: you turn the story a founder tells in a room into a page an investor reads alone. Short, plain, in a founder's voice, with numbers that held under diligence.

  • Modelling: you built an investor model from a company's internal forecast and defended it in diligence.

  • Terms: you can put two term sheets side by side and say what each costs in the round after.

  • Data rooms: you built one that answered questions before they were asked. You can name the question you missed.

  • Getting work from other teams: you got inputs from teams that did not report to you, on dates agreed in writing. You can say what arrived late and what you did about it.

  • Market knowledge: you know which funds invest at our stage and which partner leads, or can build that picture in weeks and show your working.

  • Handling no: investors have told you no. You kept the record of why and used it the next time.

Nice to have

  • Experience in logistics, delivery, marketplaces or another operations-heavy business.

  • Time at a growth-stage fund, a tech-focused bank or a private-capital adviser before going in-house.

  • Investor relations between rounds at a private company.

The hard parts

  • The CEO pitches. You are the investors' contact for everything around the room. You are judged on how the round runs, not on the pitch.

  • The numbers come from the CFO. The proof comes from teams that do not report to you.

  • The market sets the timing, not us.

  • Investors will say no, often. The record has to stay straight.

  • The job keeps going after the close: the map, the materials in quiet quarters and the relationships between rounds. We will agree with you what support you need to do that well.

How we hire

  1. Talent Acquisition, 45 minutes: the job as it is, a round you ran or worked on, and how you work.

  2. An interview with our VP International: 45 minutes: how you work, the evidence and across your whole career

  3. The case, about a day on your own time

  4. Case review, 75 minutes, with the CEO and CFO: you walk us through it, re-plan live when we change a condition, and take two questions the case cannot reach .

  5. References and a decision within a week. An offer comes in a conversation.

Tell us at any stage if you need adjustments.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Head of Compliance and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

  • Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

  • Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

  • Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

  • Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

Head of Digital Commerce DACH (all genders)

 

Your Role & Impact

You lead the Marketplace and E-Commerce team and report to the General Manager DACH. Today that’s a small, high-impact team of two (E-Commerce Manager, Marketplace Manager), with the team expected to grow to around 4-5 people next year. You think strategically, but you're also hands-on and ready to step in operationally when needed.

 

What you'll do

  • Trading & Promotion: Own the DACH digital promotion calendar and drive data-driven trading, conversion and content optimisation.

  • Planning with Finance & Operations: Own the digital budget and forecasting cycle; align stock planning and pre-order/launch quantities.

  • Assortment & Activation with Portfolio and Marketing: Align digital assortment, online pricing and launch phasing; steer traffic, CRM and content.

  • Global Interface: Act as the primary DACH counterpart to Global DTC Coordination (CRO Org) on platform strategy and the tonies.com roadmap.

  • P&L Ownership: Own net revenue, contribution margin and media efficiency across all digital channels.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on commercial ownership experience in digital channels (pricing, trading, assortment and channel strategy), built through running e-commerce/marketplace operations yourself

title: Head of Electronics & software
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Head of Electronics & Software

Purpose

We are looking for a Head of Electronics & Software to lead and develop the engineering capability behind some of the most critical systems in our spacecraft.

This is a senior leadership role combining people leadership, engineering excellence, organisational development and technical breadth. You will lead a multidisciplinary organisation spanning:

  • Avionics, communications and electrical power systems

  • Flight software (FSW)

  • Guidance, navigation and control (GNC)

  • Electrical wiring and interconnection systems (EWIS), including harness engineering

  • Future projects and advanced electronics and software development

You will be responsible for ensuring our teams have the people, skills, processes, tools and engineering standards needed to deliver ambitious space programmes today, while building the capabilities we will need for the future.

This is not a role for someone looking to step away from engineering. We are looking for a leader who can engage credibly with highly technical teams, challenge constructively, develop strong technical leaders and help create an environment where exceptional engineering can happen.

Matrix Organisation

Our engineering teams work in a matrix organisation, combining strong functional leadership with project-based delivery.

As Head of Electronics & Software, you will lead the functional organisation, developing its people and capabilities while working closely with Project Managers, Project Chief Engineers, technical authorities and engineering Leads responsible for programme delivery.

You will:

  • Lead and develop Project Leads, discipline Leads, Principal Engineers and transversal engineering resources

  • Partner with project leadership to align capability, resources and priorities with programme needs

  • Help teams navigate competing priorities across projects

  • Ensure clear ownership and accountability between functional leadership and project execution

  • Build an organisation capable of supporting multiple programmes as the company grows

Success in this environment requires collaboration, influence and sound engineering judgement rather than centralising every technical decision.

Role Boundaries

This role owns the strength and effectiveness of the Electronics & Software organisation: its people, capability, engineering practices, tools, standards and functional budget.

You will create the environment in which our technical teams can perform at their best, providing mentoring, challenge and access to expertise while supporting technical and project leadership in making strong engineering decisions.

Project technical decisions and product technical authority remain within the relevant project and technical organisations. Your role is to ensure they are supported by a highly capable engineering organisation with the right expertise, methods and resources.

Key Responsibilities

People, Hiring & Organisation

You will build and shape a high-performing Electronics & Software organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning workforce and headcount planning across the function

  • Recruiting and retaining exceptional engineering talent

  • Developing clear job families, role levels and assessment standards

  • Partnering with Talent Acquisition, engineering Leads and hiring managers to maintain a high technical hiring bar

  • Leading promotion, compensation and organisational planning within the function

  • Building succession plans and reducing key-person dependencies in specialist areas

  • Creating an organisation that remains lean, scalable and aligned with current and future programme needs

Line Management & Development

Developing strong engineers and technical leaders will be a major part of the role.

You will:

  • Lead and develop the managers, Leads and senior engineers within your organisation

  • Establish meaningful objectives aligned with project and company priorities

  • Build clear development and technical career paths

  • Strengthen mentoring, coaching and leadership capability across the organisation

  • Create opportunities for engineers to gain experience across design, integration, test and operations

  • Address performance challenges fairly and constructively

  • Build a culture where progression is based on demonstrated capability, impact and organisational need

Engineering Processes, Standards & Compliance

You will help define how excellent electronics and software engineering is done across the company.

This includes:

  • Owning and continuously improving engineering practices across electronics, software, GNC and electrical/harness engineering

  • Establishing practical standards for electronics design, software development, testing, modelling, reviews and verification

  • Ensuring teams understand and can effectively apply the relevant processes

  • Supporting certification readiness, audits and continuous improvement, including applicable EN9100 requirements

  • Working closely with Quality, Safety, Systems Engineering and the Chief Engineer organisation

  • Using lessons from development, testing and operations to continuously improve engineering practices

Our aim is not process for process's sake. We want processes that are lean, pragmatic and proportionate to engineering risk.

Engineering Tools & Ways of Working

You will ensure our engineers have the tools and engineering environment needed to work effectively and at scale.

This includes capability across:

  • Electronics and PCB design

  • Harness CAD

  • Software development, build and configuration toolchains

  • Automated testing

  • GNC analysis and modelling

  • Software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop environments

  • Simulation and shared test infrastructure

You will drive standardisation, adoption and good engineering practice while partnering with Digital, IT, Procurement, Quality and other engineering teams.

The goal is simple: engineering work should be efficient, traceable, reproducible and ready to scale.

Project Support & Resource Planning

You will work closely with our projects to ensure they have access to the Electronics & Software capability they need.

You will:

  • Mentor engineering Leads and provide senior technical guidance where needed

  • Support major technical and engineering reviews

  • Maintain visibility of capability gaps, resource constraints and significant engineering risks

  • Work with project leadership to resolve resource requirements through hiring, development, internal mobility or external support

  • Anticipate future capacity constraints before they become programme blockers

  • Help resolve cross-project resource and organisational conflicts

  • Contribute to the company-wide electronics and software strategy alongside the Chief of Engineering and CTO

  • Shape future capabilities, reusable technologies, R&D priorities and obsolescence strategies

Budget

You will own the Electronics & Software functional budget and forecast, including:

  • Headcount and personnel planning

  • Engineering tools and licences

  • Relevant shared simulation and test capability

  • Training and development

  • Functional team travel

You will work closely with Finance, Procurement, Digital and project leadership to ensure investment supports both immediate programme needs and longer-term engineering capability.

Requirements

We are looking for someone who combines credible engineering depth with proven organisational leadership.

You should bring:

  • Strong hands-on engineering experience in at least one of the following: avionics, electronics, embedded systems, flight software, GNC or electrical systems

  • Enough technical breadth to operate effectively across several of these disciplines and understand how they interact

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a complex product environment

  • Proven formal line-management experience, including developing managers and technical leaders

  • Experience hiring, developing and building engineering organisations

  • Experience with organisational design, workforce and capacity planning

  • Experience creating or improving engineering processes, tools, standards and ways of working

  • Experience operating within a matrix organisation and supporting multiple projects or programmes

  • Strong coaching, mentoring, communication and influencing skills

  • The technical credibility to challenge senior engineers while empowering the appropriate technical owners to make decisions

  • A pragmatic approach to engineering quality, assurance and compliance, including relevant EN9100 practices

Experience in spacecraft, launch vehicles, aerospace, defence, aviation, robotics or another complex safety-critical engineering environment would be particularly relevant.

We are looking for a leader who:

  • Leads with high standards, humility and low ego

  • Enjoys developing people rather than simply directing them

  • Empowers strong technical Leads and avoids becoming a bottleneck

  • Can challenge experienced engineers constructively

  • Makes decisions using data and sound engineering judgement

  • Balances immediate programme pressures with long-term organisational capability

  • Creates clarity where responsibilities cross organisational boundaries

  • Promotes transparency, accountability, collaboration and continuous learning

  • Believes in extreme ownership and engineering first principles

  • Remains close enough to the engineering to understand the challenges our teams are solving

Location & Travel

This is a leadership role with teams and stakeholders across our European organisation, so regular face-to-face engagement is important.

You should expect to spend time across our main European sites, with additional travel where required for team leadership, recruitment, major engineering reviews, audits and project support.

title: Head of Finance (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über diese Rolle

Du willst nicht nur Zahlen berichten, sondern mitentscheiden, wie ein Unternehmen wächst?

Als Head of Finance (m/w/d) sorgst du dafür, dass wir jederzeit wissen, wo wir finanziell stehen: wie viel Liquidität wir haben, mit welchen Produkten und Kanälen wir Geld verdienen und wie viel wir in Marketing, Ware und neue Märkte investieren können. Du lieferst die Zahlen, auf deren Basis wir entscheiden, und sorgst dafür, dass unser Wachstum solide finanziert ist.

Wir sind ein schnell wachsendes E-Commerce Scale Up mit Sitz in der Speicherstadt Hamburg. Unsere Mission ist es, Kinder mit innovativen Produkten für das lebenslange Lernen zu begeistern und das Leben von Millionen Familien liebevoller und bunter zu gestalten.

Bewirb dich jetzt und gestalte aktiv die Zukunft eines dynamischen Unternehmens mit!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Liquidität & Cashflow: Du verantwortest unsere rollierende Liquiditätsplanung, damit wir jederzeit wissen, wie viel Geld für Marketing, Wareneinkauf und Saisonspitzen zur Verfügung steht.

  • P&L & Controlling: Du pflegst unsere monatliche P&L auf und zeigst mit dem Deckungsbeitrag von DB1 bis DB4, mit welchen Produkten und Kanälen wir Geld verdienen.

  • Abschluss & Finanzierung: Du verantwortest Bilanz und Jahresabschluss gemeinsam mit dem Steuerberater und führst die Gespräche mit Banken und Finanzierungspartnern.

  • Automatisierung: Du automatisierst unsere Finance-Prozesse, damit die Zahlen schnell und verlässlich vorliegen.

Dein Profil

  • Du hast mindestens 5+ Jahre Erfahrung in Finance oder Controlling, idealerweise davon mehrere Jahre in einer 8-stelligen D2C E-Commerce Brand.

title: Director of Growth (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
About enua

enua is an integrated medical cannabis company with a mission to give patients safe and reliable access to treatment. We are the second-largest supplier in the German market and a fast-growing international group, on track for around €100m in group revenue in 2026 with a double-digit EBITDA margin. Founded in Cologne in 2018, we have built a profitable business across our own products and more than 700 partner pharmacies.

Now we are bringing that to the UK. Medical cannabis is one of the fastest-growing areas of UK healthcare: around 140,000 people will be prescribed it in 2026, up from around 100,000 a year earlier. Yet an estimated 1.8 million people in the UK already use cannabis to manage a health condition, mostly outside the legal system. That is more than 10x today’s market, in a category that is still largely uncharted.

We are building a clinic and platform that makes care simpler, faster and more personal. Our UK team is at an early stage, which means real ownership, real impact and the chance to shape how we work from day one.

The role

  • Location: London, 4 days a week in the office

  • Reporting to: MD and Co-Founder UK

  • Employment type: Full-time, permanent

As Director of Growth, you will lead growth for enua UK: building our patient acquisition engine and shaping how the UK talks about medical cannabis as a legitimate treatment. This is a highly commercial, founding leadership role in the UK.

You will own our growth strategy and budget, with the mandate to build the team and infrastructure to deliver it. You will sit on a small management team with our MD and Co-Founder, jointly responsible for the success of the business, and have a real say in product, pricing and go-to-market decisions.

Tasks

  • Leadership: Be a core member of our management team, jointly responsible for setting and delivering the strategy for the business. Build a high-performing, AI-first marketing team and get the best from our agencies and freelancers.

  • Growth strategy and execution: Own the growth plan and budget. With the MD, set and deliver our patient acquisition strategy, including which channels we use and how much we invest in each. Partner with product and tech to improve conversion across our website and sign-up flow, and evolve our brand positioning as we learn from patients.

  • Long-term value: Drive total net long-term value from every patient we acquire, optimising CAC, average revenue per patient and retention together. Focus on acquiring the right patients, not just more of them. Set targets and budgets with finance based on unit economics.

  • Performance marketing: Own performance across all channels, including search and SEO, paid social, affiliates, partnerships, referral, offline and print.

  • Tracking and reporting: Set up attribution, tracking and reporting from scratch, so every pound of spend is accountable, and report weekly on performance.

  • Category awareness and PR: Build awareness and trust in medical cannabis and help reduce stigma. Set our PR strategy with our agency partners.

  • CRM and retention: Shape the patient CRM journey to drive engagement and retention, working closely with our clinical team.

Requirements

  • A strategic, AI-first leader: 7+ years in marketing, with at least 3 in a senior or Head of role. You have led a team of 3 or more, been part of a leadership team and embedded AI in how a team works.

  • Experienced performance marketer: Strong hands-on experience across search, SEO, paid social and funnel optimisation, with a track record of scaling spend at a healthy CAC and LTV:CAC. Partnerships experience is a real bonus.

  • A builder: You have been an early hire in a founding team and helped take a consumer business from launch through rapid scale, building the growth engine rather than inheriting it.

  • Sector-savvy: Background in D2C subscription, consumer health or another regulated category (healthcare, pharma, telehealth or similar), with a good grasp of repeat-purchase economics, CRM and advertising within the rules.

  • Commercially sharp: You think in unit economics and long-term value, can explain the numbers to non-marketers and make every pound work.

  • A proactive driver of growth: You test, learn and adapt quickly without waiting to be asked.

Benefits

  • Define a new category: Medical cannabis is still young in the UK. You will shape how patients, clinicians and the public see it, and set the standard for what great looks like.

  • Build it with the founding team: A seat on our small management team from day one, working side by side with our MD and Co-Founder.

  • Real ownership: Your own budget, your own plan and the mandate to build the team and partners to deliver it.

  • A fast-growing market: Patient numbers are growing by around 40% a year, with more than 10x headroom still to come.

  • Serious backing: The support of a profitable European healthcare group with real credentials in products, pharmacy and telemedicine.

We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Excited but not sure you tick every box? We would still love to hear from you. If you need any reasonable adjustments during the process, just let us know.

title: Head of Investment Fund Operations
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly experienced Head of Fund Operations to oversee the operational management of a diverse Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio within an established international private banking environment.

In this responsible leadership role, you will manage a small team of fund operations specialists and ensure reliable, accurate and efficient processes across fund data, cost management, NAV controls and reporting. You will work closely with internal stakeholders as well as fund administrators, system providers, auditors, tax advisors and other external partners. As a member of the Valuation Committee, you will also contribute your expertise to fund valuation-related decisions.

The position offers a combination of team leadership, fund operations expertise, data management, regulatory knowledge and process automation, with considerable scope to improve existing processes and further professionalise the operational setup.

Location: Basel

Your Responsibilities:

  • Manage and develop a team of three Fund Operations specialists and oversee operations for the complete Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio

  • Ensure the availability, integrity and quality of fund data across the relevant internal systems

  • Monitor end-to-end data flows and act as the key contact for the external system provider

  • Review and validate important fund indicators such as TER, PTR, OGC and transaction costs

  • Take ownership of the PRIIPs KID production process and ensure that the underlying information is accurate and up to date

  • Manage the relationship with CACEIS concerning NAV data, including plausibility controls and the investigation and resolution of discrepancies

  • Participate in valuation-related decisions as an active member of the Valuation Committee

  • Coordinate the preparation and publication of annual and semi-annual fund reports

  • Liaise with auditors and tax advisors and oversee relevant fund-related tax topics

  • Review fund-related invoices and ensure transparency and accuracy of associated costs

  • Coordinate the preparation of factsheets, monthly fund manager reports and regular reporting for wholesale clients

  • Analyse existing processes and identify opportunities for greater efficiency, automation and data quality

  • Drive the use of automation and data-driven approaches to improve fund operations and reporting

  • Ensure that operational processes and reporting activities are aligned with applicable Swiss and Luxembourg regulatory requirements

  • Serve as a knowledgeable and reliable contact for internal stakeholders and external service providers across fund operations

Your Profile:

  • At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in fund operations, fund controlling, fund accounting, fund administration or fund audit

  • Comprehensive knowledge of the Swiss and Luxembourg fund landscape, ideally including CISA, FINMA, AMAS, UCITS and CSSF regulations

  • Practical experience with NAV control and oversight and cooperation with external fund administrators

  • Previous experience with CACEIS is considered an advantage

  • Strong knowledge of fund reporting, data management, valuation processes and fund-related cost structures

  • Good technical capabilities, including Python or a comparable scripting language, advanced Excel and experience working with databases and SQL

  • Experience in automating operational, data or reporting processes is highly desirable

  • Strong analytical skills and a precise, structured approach to complex data and processes

  • A proactive, hands-on working style with a high degree of personal responsibility

  • Previous leadership or people management experience is an advantage

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across different functions and organisations

  • High level of integrity, reliability and accountability

  • Comfortable working in an international, regulated financial services environment

  • University or FH degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Accounting or a comparable discipline

  • Excellent English skills; German and French are advantageous

What We Offer:

  • A senior position with broad responsibility for the operational management of a Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio

  • The opportunity to shape and further improve the Fund Operations function and its processes

  • A varied role combining leadership, fund operations, data and automation

  • Regular interaction with senior internal stakeholders and key external partners

  • The opportunity to contribute to the Valuation Committee and support important fund-related decisions

  • Significant scope to introduce process improvements and strengthen automation and data quality

  • An international environment within an established and reputable private banking organisation

  • Flexible working arrangements and a modern working environment

  • Opportunities for continued professional and personal development

title: Head of Product – SAP (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Almost every company running SAP faces the same task: the move to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point. Nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades. That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI platform for S/4HANA transformation. Qorelo reads code, processes, documentation and how the system is actually used, makes the existing landscape transparent, and delivers the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. We take a clean core, target-architecture-first approach and carry it end to end across SAP Activate, from Discover to Realize. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards, long after the system integrators have moved on. We've raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies, including Mercedes-Benz.

The role We are looking for our first Head of Product. You own what Qorelo builds and why, and you build the product function around it. You lead our solution architects, the people who carry our SAP domain depth, you work hand in hand with our Head of Product Design and the engineering team, and you report directly to the C-level. This is a leadership role at an early-stage company, which means two things at once. You set product strategy and make the big roadmap calls together with the founders, and you still write the spec, sit in the customer workshop and draw the cut line when it matters. Your decisions show up in the product within weeks, running inside some of the largest SAP landscapes in Europe.

What you'll own • Product strategy. Where Qorelo goes across the transformation lifecycle, which problems we solve first and which we deliberately leave to others. You turn that into a roadmap the whole company understands. • The roadmap and the calls behind it. You prioritise with evidence from customers, Proofs of Value and the market, and you can defend every call to the founders, to sales and to engineering. • The product team. You lead our two solution architects today and grow the product team as we scale: hiring, coaching and setting the bar. • Discovery with real users. Consultants, SAP leads and transformation teams use Qorelo inside live programmes. You and your team sit with them, see where the product wins and where it falls short, and bring that back as decisions, not just notes. • Product in the sales cycle. You join key customer and partner conversations, shape Proofs of Value with sales, and make sure what we promise matches what we ship. • The bridge between SAP and AI. SAP depth on one side, an AI-native engineering team on the other. You speak enough of both languages that nothing gets lost, and together with our solution architects you make sure what we ship is usable by SAP people, not just correct. • Shipping and outcomes. Specs, acceptance criteria, tradeoffs, cut lines and success metrics. Features reach real users on real landscapes, and you own whether they landed.

What you need
• 6+ years of professional experience, with deep hands-on SAP experience: S/4HANA transformation, fit-to-standard, and module-level depth in at least one core area such as FI/CO, SD, MM or PP. Whether you come from SAP consulting, solution architecture or product at an SAP ecosystem software company, all of it counts.
• 4+ years in product: you've owned a B2B product and its roadmap end to end, prioritised with engineering and shipped to enterprise users. Title doesn't matter, ownership does.
• Experience leading people: you have led product managers, solution architects or consultants, and you want to keep building a team.
• A command of the SAP transformation lifecycle and SAP Activate deep enough to be credible with CIOs, Heads of SAP and senior consultants at enterprise clients.
• Strong AI curiosity: you've actually built or worked hands-on with LLM tooling and formed opinions about where it breaks.
• Comfort in an early-stage environment: ambiguity, speed, hands-on work alongside strategy.
• Fluent English. German is a plus for our DACH client base, but not expected.

• You've sat inside an S/4HANA programme and thought "half of this should be software", and you can name which half.

title: Head of Solution Consulting R&D / Field CSO
descriptionHtml:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW

R&D leaders trust people who have done the science. More than half of the world's top 50 biopharma companies already use Benchling, and many of the most important are in Europe. Our ambition is 10x faster science, from idea to first dose. With Science Foundries, launched at Benchtalk 2026, agents and scientists run entire R&D workflows together, so a three-person team can have the productive capacity of thirty.

In a senior R&D role, you can change how one organisation does science. As our Field CSO, you'll take one question to R&D organisations across EMEA: how do we get from idea to first dose 10x faster?

ROLE OVERVIEW

You'll lead our EMEA R&D Solution Consulting organisation: a team of 12, with two first-line leaders covering our Enterprise and Strategic segments, plus occasional support for APAC deals. You'll be the scientific counterpart to our General Manager, EMEA, and work alongside our Field CTO. They lead on IT, data science and architecture; you lead on the scientists and how their work changes.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Be the scientific voice in the room. Brief the GM and account teams before key meetings, then join them as a peer to the CSOs and Heads of R&D across the table. Act as senior sponsor on our largest EMEA opportunities, and use account-team introductions to open new R&D relationships.

  • Lead the 10x conversation. Turn Benchling's vision, from AI agents to Science Foundries, into a credible plan R&D leaders can act on, including how their scientists move onto Benchling and what changes in the lab.

  • Lead and develop two first-line leaders and their team of 10. Provide in-region leadership continuity, set the scientific bar for every customer engagement, and build a succession plan as the team grows.

  • Shape EMEA strategy and the roadmap. Decide with sales leadership where to focus the team's expertise, and bring patterns from the field back to Product, Marketing and global Solution Consulting.

HOW WE'LL MEASURE SUCCESS

This is a commercial role with a scientific core. We'll look at EMEA revenue growth and influenced pipeline, technical win rate, forecast accuracy on the technical side of deals, regional ownership of our largest R&D relationships, and the strength of your leadership bench.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Substantial hands-on R&D experience in biotech or pharma, with a PhD or equivalent scientific depth. You've run experiments, led programmes and know how large R&D organisations make decisions and adopt change.

  • A record of driving change, from adopting new technologies to rethinking how your teams work, and clear views on how AI will change R&D.

  • Experience leading through other managers, and executive presence with VPs, Heads of R&D and C-level leaders.

  • Commercial ambition and a growth mindset. We'll teach you how software is sold. We can't teach how a large R&D organisation works from the inside, and that's what you bring.

  • Readiness for a field role: frequent on-site time with the largest pharma and biotech companies across EMEA, plus US travel three to four times a year for team offsites and our global sales kickoff.

  • Fluency in English; German or French is a plus.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with Benchling or a comparable R&D platform (ELN, LIMS or R&D data platform), including leading its evaluation or rollout

  • Customer-facing scientific, internal consulting, or CRO/CDMO programme leadership roles

  • Presales or solution consulting experience

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

title: Head of Strategy & Operations
descriptionHtml:
About remove

remove is a non-profit organisation with a mission to enable innovators globally to realize the "net" in net zero. remove has established premier global startup accelerator programs focused solely on Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) across Europe, India, Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America. To date, we have supported over 200 startups and cultivated a global CDR community. We also develop CDR ecosystems and engage in strategic projects to close systemic gaps in carbon removal globally. We are a small, remote team that works like a startup: high standards, an agile approach and a lot of ownership per person. Our work is funded by leading climate foundations and philanthropic partners such as The Grantham Foundation for the Protection of the Environment, Postcode Loterij Fonds and VP Capital.

About the role

We are looking for a senior professional to lead strategy and operations at remove, managing our talent and running the engine that keeps us moving. You will work very closely with our two co-founders, manage our program managers, and be the person who makes sure the right things get done, well and on time, as we grow our impact in new ways and into new regions at a pivotal stage of our organization.

What you will own

Strategy

  • Lead strategic thinking, be a sounding board to the co-founders, and the person who "writes the strategy down" and plans for its execution.

  • Prepare and run strategy days, offsites and team meetups.

  • Own key strategic documents and shape important external documents.

Planning and Operations

  • Develop and own our roadmap and workplans. Keep everyone accountable to shared goals and spot early and proactively when plans need to change.

  • Own our operating rhythm: recurring meetings, brainstorms, 1:1s, team updates, retros and milestone planning.

  • Develop and improve the processes and documentation the team relies on, including program SOPs and team policies.

People and team

  • Line-manage our program managers: debottleneck daily operations, set priorities, manage workload, coach the team, manage development plans, etc.

  • Lead hiring and onboarding for new team members and external support, and plan team capacity as we grow. We are not expecting to grow team members in large numbers; we intend to remain a lean and mighty team.

  • Look after team health and ways of working in a fully remote, multicultural team.

Fundraising operations

  • Run the process behind the co-founders’ fundraising efforts.

  • Maintain and develop core materials such as our decks, concept notes and one-pagers, and draft or coordinate grant applications.

  • Own impact reporting content and contribute to funder reports.

Strategic projects & programs

  • Scope & lead strategic initiatives from idea to delivery, alongside recurring work.

  • Oversee our programs and systems as we expand.

  • Oversee our entity’s brand and communications.

Who you are

You must have

  • 12+ years of experience, including roles where you ran strategy, operations and/or a PMO for a leadership team. You have done this job before with a laser focus on high standards and timely execution. You don’t let things fall through the cracks.

  • Experience supporting fundraising or business development, e.g. pipelines, proposals and reporting.

  • A track record of managing people well, ideally in small remote teams.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You can build structure where there is none and adjust it as things change.

  • Resourcefulness and agency. You see what needs doing and do it without waiting to be asked, including the unglamorous parts. You have an entrepreneurial spirit and drive in conceptualising and executing initiatives, with strong organisational and documentation skills.

  • Excellent communication, writing and synthesis. You can turn a messy conversation into a clear plan, deck or proposal.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and persuade diverse groups, in a cross-cultural remote setting.

  • Ability to work autonomously in a remote workspace, meeting deadlines and managing several work streams simultaneously.

  • Adaptability, curiosity and eagerness to keep learning in a dynamic environment.

  • Ability to speak and write in English fluently.

  • Willingness to travel locally or occasionally regionally/globally, if necessary.

It is a plus if you have

  • A university degree (MSc. preferred) in a relevant field (e.g. environmental science, engineering, sustainability, business administration)

  • Experience in and a strong passion for climate action, carbon removal or the wider sustainability field.

  • Experience with accelerators, startups or entrepreneurship programs.

  • Experience with foundations or philanthropic funding.

  • Experience working in or with partners in the Global South.

  • A coaching or facilitation background.

Practicalities

  • This role reports to the two co-founders.

  • Location: remote, in Europe. Preference will be given to those based in Northwestern Europe due to proximity to the co-founders. Occasional travel for team meetups and selected events.

  • Contract: full time, with start date April 1, 2027. Depending on your location, you may be employed through an employer-of-record provider. You must be able to work in your country of residence. We will not sponsor visas or work permits.

  • Salary: competitive for non-profit salary bands for small teams in your location.

What we offer

  • A flexible and fully remote workplace.

  • An impact-driven role as part of a mission-driven team and organisation working with entrepreneurs globally.

  • A unique opportunity to experience and shape strategy for a future billion-dollar industry in its early days.

  • Exposure to a great network and community of CDR innovators and experts.

  • A learning budget to develop yourself.

  • Flexible holidays and biannual team off-sites.

How to apply

Submit your CV and a short cover letter (no more than one page) detailing your relevant experience and why you believe you would be the ideal candidate for the role. We will review applications on a rolling basis and aim to start interviews as soon as possible, latest by mid November 2026.

Our process:

  • First step after screening: Role-related interview with Rawan Gebran (Senior Director @ remove) - ~30 min

  • Next: Interview panel with both co-founders, Hans Westerhof & Marian Krueger - ~45 min

  • Then: 1:1 interviews with each of the founders individually - ~45 min each

  • Finally: Shortlisted candidates will be asked for 3 references willing to speak about their experience with you, professionally and in that time could meet the rest of the team.

If you’ve built and run the strategic and operating backbone for a small and agile team before and want to do it for the organization helping CDR startups globally get off the ground, we want to hear from you! We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Design the delivery solution for every new mobilisation

  • Take the client's requirements from Sales and put forward the delivery solution for each mobilisation proposal.

  • Agree rates and SLAs with the contractors and negotiate on deliverables and pricing.

Own contractor performance across the network

  • Own SLA attainment, aged WIP and escalations across our contractor network.

Lead the contractor account management team

  • Accountable for contractor monthly account management calls covering KPIs, aged WIP plans, pricing and quote health, capacity and growth, and platform adoption.

Build strategic contractor relationships

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Experience leading and developing a team, with clear goals and regular performance conversations.

title: HR Manager
descriptionHtml:
About 3E:

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. 

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About the Role

3E is growing, and with the recent acquisition of the Yordas Group, we have an exciting opportunity to shape how our UK teams come together and work as part of a broader global organization. We’re looking for an experienced HR Manager who can play a key role in integration today while helping build the strong, scalable HR practices that will support our teams well beyond the transition.

As a trusted, hands-on partner to employees and leaders, you’ll help people navigate change while ensuring day-to-day HR operations run effectively. Looking beyond the integration, you’ll work closely with colleagues across our global HR organization to strengthen people practices, improve processes and systems, and contribute to regional and global initiatives as the role evolves.

This role requires a regular presence in our Lancaster office, with a minimum of three days onsite each week. Being close to the teams you support will help you build strong relationships, understand the local organization and culture, and provide responsive, effective HR support.

If you enjoy building relationships, improving how things work, and helping people navigate change, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution during an important transition and help shape the future of HR operations at 3E.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as a trusted HR advisor to UK employees, managers, and leaders on employee relations, performance management, absence, grievances, disciplinary matters, and workplace investigations.

  • Help employees and managers navigate organizational changes, including integration activities, new HR processes, benefits changes, communications, and culture initiatives.

  • Manage complex employee relations matters with appropriate judgment, documentation, and alignment with UK employment law and company policies.

  • Oversee key HR operations across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, employee changes, leave administration, benefits, and employee records.

  • Serve as a UK subject matter resource for payroll-related legislation and statutory requirements, partnering with Finance, the regional HR team, and external payroll providers.

  • Manage regional HR and benefits vendors, resolving issues and helping ensure employees receive responsive, high-quality support.

  • Maintain and improve HR policies, procedures, employee resources, and documentation in line with employment legislation and business needs.

  • Monitor changes in employment legislation and help ensure HR practices remain compliant.

  • Maintain accurate HRIS data and employee records and support HR reporting and analysis.

  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Talent Acquisition, local leadership, and regional HR colleagues on employment, compliance, recruitment, payroll, and people initiatives.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify and improve HR processes, systems, and workflows.

  • Create and maintain SOPs and share knowledge across the HR team to strengthen consistency and business continuity.

  • Contribute to regional and global HR projects as the organization continues to grow and evolve.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Required

  • 10+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 2–3 years of HR Manager-level experience supporting regional or multi-country HR operations.

  • Strong knowledge of UK employment law and HR practices, with the ability to translate requirements into practical guidance for employees and managers.

  • Significant hands-on employee relations experience, including managing complex or sensitive employee matters.

  • Experience independently managing complex HR processes with strong attention to accuracy and compliance.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including experience advising and supporting managers.

  • Comfortable working in a global, matrixed environment and collaborating with colleagues across functions and geographies.

  • Able to navigate ambiguity, changing priorities, and organizational change while exercising sound judgment.

  • A continuous-improvement mindset with experience identifying and implementing improvements to HR processes.

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.

  • High integrity and discretion when handling sensitive and confidential information.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot to improve the efficiency or quality of your work.

  • Fluency in written and spoken English.

  • Ability to work from our Lancaster office a minimum of three days per week.

Preferred

  • CIPD or equivalent qualification.

  • Additional language skills, such as Turkish, German, or French.

  • Experience supporting HR operations in a high-growth, matrixed organization.

  • Experience contributing to or leading HR projects and initiatives in a dynamic, global environment.

title: Human Data Collection Associate
descriptionHtml:
Type: Full-time ·

Location: London, UK · On-site

Compensation: £50,000–£65,000/year, in accordance with experience ·

The Role

We're building a foundation model of the brain and behaviour across species, and the data that powers it is produced in-house by a small, high-trust team. This role sits at the centre of that effort. As a Human Data Collection Associate, you run data collection sessions on assigned rigs, preparing and calibrating the setup, running the session, and making sure the data you hand off is clean and complete.

It is a hands-on role with real ownership. You'll report to the Human Data Collection Lead and work alongside the Hardware Systems team who build and maintain the rigs. You'll also take part in sessions as a contributor of your own data, so comfort being recorded during collection is part of the role.

Responsibilities

Running data collection

  • Prepare, calibrate, and run recording sessions from start to finish, following defined protocols precisely

  • Fit sensors, verify signal quality in real time, and resolve issues before they affect a session

  • Contribute your own data as a session participant where the protocol calls for it

Data quality and integrity

  • Own the quality bar for everything you collect. Review, label, and validate recordings so that only clean, well-documented data moves downstream

  • Keep accurate consent, provenance, and session-metadata records for every dataset, following the standards the Lead sets and our obligations under UK GDPR

  • Identify and document anomalies, and help refine protocols as we learn what works

Operations and equipment

  • Keep your recording setup maintained, charged, and ready, and track its condition over time

  • Support session scheduling and keep collection running smoothly day to day

  • Help onboard and coordinate short-term participants as we scale collection

Requirements

Core (essential)

  • Meticulous attention to detail and real care for data quality

  • Able to follow structured, repeatable protocols precisely and consistently

  • Confident with hands-on technical setups and quick to troubleshoot when something is not working

  • Reliable and organised, able to own a process from end to end with minimal oversight

  • Comfortable taking part in data collection sessions as a contributor, including being recorded

  • Strong interpersonal skills, with a knack for putting participants at ease

  • Right to work in the UK

Valued

  • Experience in a research, lab, clinical, or data collection setting

  • Familiarity with physiological or behavioural recording equipment

  • Exposure to biosignal or time-series data, and basic comfort with data tools such as spreadsheets or light scripting

  • Genuine interest in neuroscience, AI, or the science of human and animal behaviour

  • Experience maintaining quality standards and documentation in a high-rigour environment
